comparison: Perfect alignment on experimental design and data quality (C26-C30). Both evaluations accept the library design, methodology, and quality metrics without concern. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation while peer reviewers note the dataset was previously published and accept the categorical data approach.

Complete agreement on model structure and validation (C31-C35). Both evaluations strongly support the model's rigor and predictive accuracy. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the reference-free approach and predict the method will be valuable to the community, aligning with OpenEval's positive assessment of model validity.

Strong alignment on genetic architecture findings (C4-C5, C36-C37, C40-C42). Both evaluations support the dominance of low-order effects. OpenEval adds cautionary notes about interpreting higher-order epistasis and methodological limitations (ordinal model precision), while peer reviewers describe findings as 'well-supported' and 'convincing' without raising these concerns. Peer review also addresses C79 (comparison to prior work) not emphasized in OpenEval R3.

Both address structural interpretations (C44-C45) and dense architecture (C43, C81). OpenEval appropriately notes these are post-hoc rationalizations rather than predictions. Peer reviewers accept the structural explanations and density findings without challenge, treating them as valid contrasts to prior sparse architecture studies.

Strong concordance on epistasis enhancing function (C46-C52, C83, C86). Both evaluations recognize this as a major, impactful finding that challenges prevailing views. Peer reviewers explicitly note the conclusion is 'impactful because many previous studies have shown that epistasis constrains evolution,' directly aligning with OpenEval's assessment that this challenges prevailing views.

Perfect alignment on mutational landscape characterization (C53-C59). Both evaluations support the findings on functional transitions, epistatic contributions, and universal sign epistasis. OpenEval adds a caveat about interpreting small-effect mutations, while peer reviewers describe analyses as 'thorough' and 'convincing' without raising concerns.

Complete agreement on epistasis's role in functional evolution (C60-C63). Both evaluations strongly support the specificity-switching findings and necessity/sufficiency analysis. OpenEval emphasizes the direct demonstration through model comparison, while peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling' without methodological concerns.

Full concordance on network analysis demonstrating epistasis facilitates evolution (C64-C70). Both evaluations accept the evolutionary simulations and network metrics. OpenEval raises a caveat about assuming equal accessibility of functional variants, which peer reviewers do not address, accepting the facilitating role without this qualification.

Perfect alignment on historical evolution findings (C71-C76). Both evaluations support the conclusions about ancestral sequences requiring epistasis and genetic architecture changing over evolution. OpenEval notes dependencies on ancestral reconstruction accuracy, while peer reviewers accept the application to historical sequences without challenge.

Strong agreement on methodological distinctions from prior work (C77-C78, C80, C82, C84-C85). Both evaluations accept the explanations for differences. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the novelty of integrating reference-free and global nonlinearity approaches, while OpenEval notes the explanations are plausible but somewhat speculative. Peer review also addresses C81 separately in R10.

Both address the main conceptual contribution about epistasis facilitating evolution (C83-C86). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of how prior work is characterized and notes context-dependency of conclusions. Peer reviewers treat this as a fundamental, well-supported finding without the caveats about generalization that OpenEval mentions.

Perfect alignment on limitations and implications (C87-C93). Both evaluations accept the author-acknowledged limitations without challenge or expansion. OpenEval describes the acknowledgments as 'appropriate' and 'important,' while peer reviewers accept the scope as stated without disputing the caveats about generalization.

Partial overlap on genetic architecture. OpenEval R3 addresses C38-C39 (epistasis and specificity) as part of broader genetic architecture findings, while peer R2 treats these specificity claims as separate, well-supported conclusions about the functional role of pairwise interactions.

OpenEval evaluates characterization of prior work in the field (C2-C3, C10-C17), finding it well-supported with extensive citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background claims about limitations in prior approaches.

OpenEval evaluates biological background on steroid hormone receptors and ancestral proteins (C18-C25), finding it well-supported by established knowledge and prior experimental work. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

Peer reviewers evaluate specificity claims (C6-C7, C38-C39) as a distinct supported finding about functional roles of pairwise interactions. OpenEval addresses C38-C39 within broader genetic architecture evaluation (R3) but does not separately evaluate C6-C7.
